blocks.content: The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG, including all salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of persons serving in that office, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

items: The removal procedure of the CAG requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament, identical to the removal of a Supreme Court judge.
Expenses related to the CAG office are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India, meaning they are not subject to a vote in Parliament.
Unlike Ministers, no Cabinet Minister can be called upon to defend or represent the CAG in Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CAG is provided with security of tenure and can be removed by the President only on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.
He is not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under any State Government after he has ceased to hold his office.
His salary and other service conditions are determined by Parliament and cannot be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG, including all salaries, allowances, and pensions, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable.
No minister can represent the Comptroller and Auditor General in Parliament or take responsibility for any administrative or audit actions performed by him.
